recent_posts.title: The keyboard used to score Dune 2 is getting more affordable
recent_posts.summary: Expressive E has announced the Osmose CE, a more affordable version of its acclaimed Osmose MPE keyboard that removes the built-in synthesizer to function as a standalone MIDI controller. Available in 49-key ($999) and 61-key ($1,199) configurations, it undercuts both the original Osmose ($1,799) and the competing Roli Seaboard 2 ($1,399). The CE version adds tighter DAW integration with Ableton Live, Bitwig, Cubase, and Logic Pro, plus a new Ctrl-e software suite with over 900 presets. The original Osmose gained fame when Hans Zimmer used an orchestra of them to score Dune: Part Two. Existing Osmose owners will receive the new software features via a future firmware update.

recent_posts.title: Govee’s multicolor ceiling light doubles as a low-res screen
recent_posts.summary: Govee has launched the Ceiling Light Ultra, a 21-inch smart ceiling light priced at $249.99. It features 616 independently controlled LEDs that can display custom images and color effects, functioning as a low-resolution screen softened by a diffuser. It outputs 5,000 lumens, supports color temperatures from 2,700 to 6,500K, and includes 100 preset lighting effects with music reactivity. The light is compatible with Matter, Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and Samsung SmartThings, and includes a new DaySync feature that adjusts brightness and color temperature to match circadian rhythms and local sunrise/sunset times.

recent_posts.title: Why people hate AI and the limits of software brain
recent_posts.summary: Nilay Patel introduces the concept of 'software brain' — a worldview that reduces everything to databases, algorithms, and automatable loops — and argues it explains the growing gap between tech industry enthusiasm for AI and widespread public hostility toward it. Polling data shows majorities of Americans, especially Gen Z, view AI negatively despite heavy usage. Patel contends AI doesn't have a marketing problem; it has a fundamental mismatch problem: tech leaders want people to flatten their lives into databases to make AI useful, but most people find this dehumanizing. He draws parallels between software thinking and legal thinking, notes the limits of both when applied to messy human reality, and argues that asking people to make themselves 'legible to software' is a doomed proposition — especially when AI executives simultaneously warn of mass job displacement.

recent_posts.title: Alienware AW2726DM QD-OLED gaming monitor hands-on impressions
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on impressions piece on the Alienware AW2726DM 27-inch 1440p QD-OLED gaming monitor priced at $350. Key highlights include a 240Hz refresh rate, semi-glossy coating, burn-in warranty, and strong contrast. The author notes QD-OLED advantages over WOLED (better uniformity, slightly better contrast) but mentions blacks can appear dark purple in bright rooms. HDR works well in games but requires manual toggling on Windows. Minor drawbacks include no USB ports and lower brightness compared to pricier panels. Overall, the author is satisfied with the purchase as a budget entry into OLED gaming.

recent_posts.title: These electronic Polaroids are powered by your phone’s NFC chip
recent_posts.summary: VidaBay's Classic Plus NFC E-Ink Fridge Magnet is a battery-free digital photo frame shaped like a Polaroid. It uses the E Ink Spectra 3100 color display — the same low-power technology found in electronic shelf price tags — and draws all its power from a smartphone's NFC chip when updating images via VidaBay's mobile app. Once an image is set, it persists indefinitely without any power. Available in white, red, or yellow for $29.99 each (discounted), the main limitation is the Spectra 3100's four-color palette (black, yellow, red, white), which produces far less accurate color reproduction compared to higher-end E Ink panels like the Spectra 6.

recent_posts.title: Razer BlackShark V2 Pro wireless gaming headset drops to new low of $90
recent_posts.summary: The Razer BlackShark V2 Pro Xbox edition wireless gaming headset is currently at a new low price of $89.99 on Amazon, down $110 from its regular price. The headset connects via Bluetooth or USB-C wireless dongle to PC, phone, tablet, Nintendo Switch 2, and other devices. Key features include 50mm drivers, detachable boom mic, SmartSwitch audio profiles, breathable memory foam cushions, and up to 70 hours of battery life on a single charge.

recent_posts.title: MacBook Neo preorder guide with pricing and retailer links
recent_posts.summary: Apple's MacBook Neo, its most affordable laptop, is available for preorder ahead of its March 11th launch. Priced at $599 for the 256GB model and $699 for the 512GB model (which adds a TouchID sensor), it features a 13-inch display, Apple's A18 Pro chip, 8GB RAM, two USB-C ports, and a 1080p camera. It lacks Thunderbolt ports and MagSafe found on the MacBook Air. Students can purchase through Apple directly for $499 and $599 respectively. Preorders are available at Apple, Amazon, B&H Photo, and Best Buy, with Best Buy offering a $25 e-gift card.

recent_posts.title: Hank Green lets loose on YouTube, billionaires, and algorithms
recent_posts.summary: Hank Green, co-founder of educational media company Complexly, discusses converting the company into a nonprofit with Nilay Patel. The conversation covers why the nonprofit structure provides insulation from profit-driven incentives that would otherwise push educational content toward paywalls and freemium models. Green reflects on YouTube's creator economy, the problems with algorithmic content recommendation, AI-generated slop, wealth inequality in tech, and why he believes liberal arts skills will matter more as AI commoditizes technical work. He argues there is abundant philanthropic capital available for educational content creators and encourages others to seek patronage rather than chase platform-driven monetization.

recent_posts.title: Siemens CEO Roland Busch’s mission to automate everything
recent_posts.summary: Siemens CEO Roland Busch discusses the company's transformation into an AI-powered automation platform spanning 320,000 employees globally. He outlines plans to automate entire factory operations using digital twins, industrial AI agents, and LLMs trained on proprietary manufacturing data. Busch addresses organizational restructuring challenges, the impact of tariffs and trade barriers on global operations, and the tension between automation's efficiency gains and workforce displacement. He emphasizes the need for domain-specific AI training to achieve industrial-grade reliability, forming data alliances with machine builders to scale model development. The conversation explores Siemens' role as a defense contractor navigating geopolitical fragmentation while maintaining optimism about global collaboration.

recent_posts.title: Experian’s tech chief defends credit scores: ‘We’re not Palantir’
recent_posts.summary: Experian's technology chief discusses how the credit reporting company uses AI for governance and model oversight rather than direct decision-making. He explains their federated organizational structure with 11,000 technologists, emphasizes privacy and security as core principles, and defends credit scoring systems as essential for economic access. The conversation covers AI implementation challenges, the use of small language models for detecting model drift in lending products, and tools like Experian Boost that help consumers improve credit scores using alternative payment data.
